assessment: The engine is finished and the kills are the ceiling, so eight of these ten answer a hole the audit measured and two widen a kill component priced at one card. Four picks buy interaction the deck does not have — the artifact class and the land class are at literal zero, and the artifact class is where Grafdigger's Cage, Cursed Totem and Null Rod live. The bench is four cards and only one of them answers a named axis: Imp's Mischief is the sole card in the box that can save a noncreature permanent, so it makes the list and the other three get a verdict line. Nine pool scouts fill the rest, ranked by ROI, and every bracket figure below was recomputed rather than asserted: the floor is 4 before and after, on all ten. Read the natural_cuts as five independent one-for-one proposals, not a swap plan.

ten.why: A turn-two Grafdigger's Cage across the table blanks the Gravecrawler recast that stacks 009 and 011 are both built on, and a regex over all 79 maindeck oracle texts finds no card that destroys or exiles an artifact at any price; Gate to Phyrexia kills the Cage on your next upkeep for {B}{B}, and again on every upkeep after that.
ten.unlocks: The artifact class, repeatably and cheaply: Cursed Totem, Null Rod, an opposing Altar, a Sensei's Divining Top all die to a creature you were sacrificing anyway. The corpus asks you to 'cover the classes — creature, artifact, enchantment, graveyard, land — before doubling any', and this is the first of the two at zero. Price it honestly: sorcery speed, once each upkeep, so it answers the hoser a turn late. The cut is Geralf's Messenger — {B}{B}{B} for a body that enters TAPPED, drains 2 from one seat, and appears in no kill's any_of and no checker-passed scenario.

ten.closes: engine single point of failure: Exquisite Blood
ten.why: Stack 012 takes a four-opponent pod from 40 to 0 on Exquisite Blood plus one lifegain-triggered drain, at 0.069 unassisted and 0.425 with a tutor, mean turn 5.301 — the fastest and likeliest kill in the deck — and the Blood half is one card against a three-card partner side.
ten.unlocks: 'Whenever an opponent loses life, you gain that much life' on a 5/5 flier with deathtouch: the one-card half becomes two, and it pairs with all three of Marauding Blight-Priest, Starscape Cleric and South Wind Avatar. It is also a creature, so Lightning Greaves can protect the kill that Exquisite Blood cannot be protected on. None of the three lines is verified. This is the page's one painful cut: Grave Titan is the deck's best single fodder card and narrows RENEWABLE FODDER from seven copies to six, but it is in no kill's any_of, the deck holds exactly two six-drops and only Mikaeus wins the game, and the stack its board appears in — 013 — already carries presentable: false.

ten.why: Protection reads 3 against a combo deck's 4-6, and the defect is shape: Lightning Greaves, Sedgemoor Witch and Yahenni all protect a creature, while the drain that loops in stacks 009, 010 and 011 is Bastion of Remembrance, an enchantment, and the mana in 011 is Phyrexian Altar, an artifact.
ten.when: Sleeve it against any pod holding single-target noncreature removal, and against blue — for {1}{B} at instant speed it points the Krosan Grip somewhere else and answers the counterspell aimed at your Beseech the Mirror, paying only that spell's mana value in life. Leave it in the box against wipes and Cyclonic Rift: the redirect needs a spell with exactly one target and a second legal target to move it to. No cut is offered because none is needed — the corpus's own advice for a bench is to 'keep the near-misses as a sideboard and swap them in between games'.

ten.why: Land is the deck's other class at zero and Strip Mine closes it out of a land slot rather than a spell slot — 36 land copies before and 36 after — with colour-sources six above the Karsten target, so the black source is affordable.
ten.unlocks: An answer to the Cabal Coffers, Nykthos, Glacial Chasm or Maze of Ith that is beating you on turn five, and a colourless tap the other nineteen games. Warn yourself once: card_roles files it land:utility, so the breadth axis will keep reading 2 with the land class covered, exactly as it already does for Bojuka Bog and the graveyard class — judge this one by the card, not by the number. The cut is Survivors' Encampment: a Desert that taps for {C}, or for a colour only by also tapping a creature, in a one-colour identity. Cut it into a land, never into a spell, or the 36-38 band breaks.

ten.why: Bastion of Remembrance is the drain inside three of the four checker-passed kills and it is one card at 0.167 by turn ten; Bontu's Monument is an each-opponent drain that fires on the CAST, which is the per-iteration event in the Warren Soultrader plus Gravecrawler loop, and it sits on an artifact that Toxic Deluge, Damnation and a Swords to Plowshares cannot reach.
ten.unlocks: A fourth member for a three-card drain group, in the one card type the pod's creature removal and enchantment removal both miss, plus {1} off every black creature spell across 28 creatures. The Soultrader line is recorded and unverified. The cut is Soul Snuffers: ignition is eight declared cards at 73.1% of which seven actually place a counter, it feeds only the bounded Nest of Scarabs engine — a value ceiling, not a kill — and Soul Snuffers is the most expensive of them at {2}{B}{B} while also shrinking your own fodder.

ten.closes: engine single point of failure: Gravecrawler
ten.why: Gravecrawler is one card at 0.165 and both unbounded kills name it; Pawn of Ulamog does not substitute for it — the audit is right about that — it removes the need for it, because a 0/1 Spawn on every nontoken death is a loop that casts nothing out of a graveyard, and the cheapest recorded version names only Reassembling Skeleton and Phyrexian Altar, both already sleeved.
ten.unlocks: Engine mana as well: that class is five cards at 61.9%, the thinnest of the class-shaped components, and every Spawn taps for {C}. Nothing here is verified — a resolve-stack run is what would settle whether the Spawn's {C} plus the Altar's {B} really pays the Skeleton's {1}{B} each iteration. The cut is Butcher Ghoul, a two-mana undying body inside KILL D's seven-card any_of; taking it narrows that group to six and leaves five Zombies besides Gravecrawler for its own cast condition.

ten.closes: engine single point of failure: Gravecrawler
ten.why: One mana for a body that returns itself from the graveyard whenever you commit a crime, and the crime is free in this deck: Blood Artist's trigger targets an opponent, so every sacrifice inside the loop pays for the next return, and Phyrexian Altar supplies the {B} it asks for.
ten.unlocks: A second Gravecrawler-free unbounded loop, at a third of the mana value, on a body the graveyard hands back. It also puts Blood Artist on a kill for the first time — the audit lists it among the drains that sit on none of the four. Say the caveat out loud: stack 004 (pass) found a single-target drain cannot take a four-player table down on the BOUNDED Nest of Scarabs engine, and that finding does not transfer to an unbounded loop, which is exactly what a stack scenario is for. No cut is offered: a one-drop is the cheapest thing on this page and the slot it wants is whichever card play tells you is dead.

ten.closes: engine single point of failure: Feed the Swarm
ten.why: The deck's entire answer to a noncreature permanent is one sorcery at 0.173 by turn ten; Withering Torment is the second copy at instant speed, killing a resolved Rest in Peace, an opposing Grave Pact or a Dictate of Erebos for three mana — McGuinness's 'essentially the most any player should pay for interaction'.
ten.unlocks: Depth on the half of that component already covered, held up on their turn rather than spent on yours. Read it as the second Feed the Swarm, not as the answer to Null Rod: it destroys a creature or an enchantment and never touches an artifact. Every creature it kills is a Bastion of Remembrance and Meathook Massacre trigger, and the synergy graph shortlists it beside both. No cut is offered — with removal already at 10 copies this is a swap for whichever spot removal your pod keeps making dead.

ten.why: The audit names it a closer for the one-card noncreature answer, and it is the only card on this page that reaches ANY nonland permanent an opponent controls — Grafdigger's Cage, Cursed Totem, Rest in Peace, an opposing Bastion — on an ETB, off a body you sacrifice afterwards for a drain trigger.
ten.unlocks: Breadth with no class restriction at all. Price it: seven mana arrives around turn ten, where mean available mana is 7.1, so it is a top-end card and not an answer you hold up. The line that makes it live is cheating it in — Animate Dead for {1}{B}, Victimize, or Persist, with Stitcher's Supplier and Plumb the Forbidden filling the graveyard — and each redeployment destroys another permanent. Ranked ninth and offered no cut: take it only when the pod's lock piece is something Gate to Phyrexia cannot reach.

ten.why: A 1/1 deathtouch Snake at the beginning of each upkeep whenever you control none — up to four bodies per turn cycle in a four-player pod, provided you eat each one before the next upkeep — which takes RENEWABLE FODDER from seven copies to eight.
ten.unlocks: The eighth copy of the class the archetype's own community would widen first, and a deathtouch blocker in front of the pod's attacker. Ranked tenth on purpose: seven copies already measure 73.6% by turn ten, the corpus prices the marginal copy at a few points ('5 copies is 31% of openers, 7 is 41%... 10 is 54%'), and the same corpus says to 'cut duplicated function before any uncovered class'. Take it only if play says the pod beats you on bodies rather than on artifacts. No cut is offered: nothing in the 99 is worth less than the breadth slots ranked above it.

bench_verdicts.why: Every mana axis on this deck is adequate or a strength — 42 sources against a Burgess target of 36, 0.919 on the turn-three land drop — so a four-mana doubler closes nothing the audit names. Urborg does make it spectacular with Cabal Coffers; that is a reason to sleeve it in a pod that reaches turn eight, not a reason to rank it against the artifact class at zero.

Flash on a second Grave Pact, and Grave Pact is already sleeved. Five mana for duplicated function while two interaction classes sit at literal zero is precisely the trade the corpus warns off: 'cut duplicated function before any uncovered class'. Bring it in against a go-wide creature pod and nowhere else.

Seven mana against 5.747 mean available mana on turn seven, in a list whose four checker-passed kills cost three to five. Every job it does is already in the 99 cheaper — Animate Dead, Persist and Victimize reanimate, Grave Pact edicts — and 28 bodies means you never needed to pay seven for one.

gaps: Not one line on this page is verified; every combo_lines_opened entry carries 'needs a stack scenario' by design. Two are worth a resolve-stack run before anything else: Bloodthirsty Conqueror plus Marauding Blight-Priest, because the whole case for the pick is that it substitutes for Exquisite Blood inside stack 012's loop and it may need an outside lifegain event the South Wind Avatar board did not; and Reassembling Skeleton plus Phyrexian Altar plus Pawn of Ulamog, because every card in it is already sleeved.

No obsoletes claim appears anywhere on this page, and one index hit was checked and rejected. obsolescence_index.json lists Sephiroth, Fabled SOLDIER as strictly better than both Mirkwood Bats and Ayara, First of Locthwain; the oracle text refutes it for this deck, because Sephiroth's drain reads 'target opponent loses 1 life' while Mirkwood Bats and Ayara both read 'each opponent'. The index measured similarity and card advantages, not reach across a four-player pod.

Two of the five natural_cuts narrow a group the goldfish measures. Butcher Ghoul is one of KILL D's seven-card non-Human any_of (seven copies to six) and Grave Titan is one of RENEWABLE FODDER's seven (also seven to six). Neither is fatal alone; re-run goldfish before sleeving both, and note that cutting Geralf's Messenger alongside Butcher Ghoul leaves five Zombies besides Gravecrawler for its cast condition.

Mirkwood Bats is the highest-value cut on the board and no entry proposes it. The audit says it is on no kill and that its drain meters on tokens, so it cannot see the nontoken Gravecrawler both recursion loops sacrifice — but stack 008 (pass) rests on it and is presentable, so cutting it takes this deck from ten presentable checker-passed lines to nine. That is an editorial call, not an analytical one, and it belongs to the pilot.

Walking Ballista is the strongest card on the shortlist that closes nothing the diagnosis names. Mikaeus, the Unhallowed is already sleeved, and the pair is a recorded two-card infinite that needs neither the commander nor a drain — a fifth kill for one slot. It stayed off because all ten above answer a measured hole; if the pilot would rather buy a kill than a fourth answer, this is the eleventh card and the ranking should be re-read from the top.

Phyrexian Tribute answers an artifact for {2}{B} and its additional cost — sacrifice two creatures — is upside in a deck paid nine ways for a death. It is not on the ten because it is one-shot and sorcery-speed where Gate to Phyrexia is repeatable, but it is castable four turns earlier than Meteor Golem and should displace Meteor Golem if the pod's hosers turn out to be Cage and Totem rather than Rest in Peace.

card-advantage reads 5 against a target of 10 and nothing here answers it, deliberately. That axis carries a probe naming five more cards whose text draws, card_roles files Necropotence as 'stax' alone, and stack 010 (pass) records the commander's own draw as mandatory and as the thing that bounds KILL D. It is a question, not a hole, and a draw spell bought against it would be a wasted slot.

The corpus has nothing on the outlet / fodder / payoff triad — the diagnosis's own open question, topping out at 0.270 similarity. Every ranking above is therefore priced against sections written for generic midrange, and the one architecture this deck actually has is the one no construction principle here can cite.
